turns.input: *stops an ordinary passer-by* "What can you tell me about Light magic?"
turns.narration:
Nicco's question hangs in the open air for a moment. The passerby—a middle-aged man with flour dusting his sleeves—regards him with mild confusion.

"Light magic?" He shakes his head. "Don't know much about magic myself, friend. The Church handles that sort of thing, don't they? You'd want a proper mage, or maybe a priest if it's prayers you're after." He glances toward the massive wooden doors of Heartstone Tower behind Nicco, then back to his face with a flicker of curiosity he doesn't voice. "Sorry I can't help you more."

He waits a moment to see if Nicco has further questions, already beginning to shift his weight as if to continue on his way.

The passer-by slows, surprised to be addressed so directly. He's a middle-aged man in a worn wool coat, carrying a cloth parcel under one arm. "Light magic?" He shakes his head slowly, glancing past Nicco toward the tower entrance as if checking for something. "Can't say I've heard of anyone practicing it. Heard the term, I suppose. Rare stuff, isn't it? The Church sorts handle anything that strange." He shrugs, shifting his parcel. "You'd want a priest for that, or someone at the market who sells books. Ordinary folk don't know much about magic workings."

He makes to continue on his way, then pauses, studying Nicco's face with a flicker of curiosity that doesn't quite become recognition or suspicion. "If you're the one asking, though, you already know more than I do. Good day to you." He dips his head and walks on, merging with the sparse foot traffic of the square.

turns.input: *stops an ordinary passer-by* "Who lives in Heartstone?"
turns.narration:
Nicco steps before an ordinary Calderan local—nothing distinguishes the passer-by but worn practical clothes and the weathered look of someone who has walked city streets for years.

The man pauses, looking up at the tower's massive wooden doors behind Nicco, then back at him with frank puzzlement. "Lives there? No one, sir. Hasn't for years." He shrugs, shifting his weight. "The old tower? Empty since I was a boy. Heartstone, they call it. Belongs to the city, or it did, or no one's sure who holds the deed now." He glances at the entrance again, perhaps wondering why this stranger asks. "Folk sometimes shelter in the square here when it rains, but inside? Door's been shut longer than I remember."

The passer-by—a middle-aged woman in a simple woolen dress, carrying a woven market basket—pauses, looking Nicco up and down with mild surprise at being addressed so directly. "Heartstone?" she repeats, glancing toward the massive wooden doors behind him. "No one, far as anyone knows. Hasn't for years." She shifts her basket to her other hip. She waits, patient but plainly eager to continue on her way, the morning sun warm on the worn cobblestones around them.

The passer-by's step falters. He glances at Nicco's face, then at the tower entrance looming behind him. "Slave auctions?" There's law offices, brokers. Not my trade."

He takes a half-step back, not quite turning away, waiting to see if Nicco has more questions or will let him pass.
